title: MOE's Directive for Schools Not to Take in Transfer Students without Required Cut-off Points
what_it_is: MOE's Directive for Schools Not to Take in Transfer Students without Required Cut-off Points

sections.label: MOE appeal cut-off point decision
sections.summary: MOE reviewed feedback and decided a simpler system would be better, considering only appeals from students who met the cut-off point.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: MOE reviewed the feedback and decided that it would be better, overall, to run a simpler system where only appeals by students who met the cut-off point would be considered.

sections.label: Successful school transfer appeals
sections.summary: Over 800 students appealed successfully and got transfers according to school preferences, most meeting the cut-off point, some not.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: With the change in the transfer guidelines, over 800 students appealed successfully and obtained a school transfer this year according to their school preferences.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Most met the school's cut-off point, while some did not, as their appeals were on the basis of medical, special needs or exceptional circumstances.

sections.label: MOE holistic education commitment
sections.summary: MOE is committed to holistic education and multiple pathways, and will study evolving admission and transfer processes while upholding meritocracy, fairness and transparency.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: MOE is committed to supporting holistic education and providing our students with multiple pathways and opportunities to pursue an education best suited to their needs and strengths.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We will continue to carefully study how we can evolve and enhance our school admission and transfer processes to support these goals while remaining consistent with our key principles of meritocracy, fairness and transparency.

sections.label: Flexibility for SACs and Principals
sections.summary: Flexibility is allowed, with about 800 students successfully transferred after making the wrong initial school choice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: With regard to the flexibility for the SACs and the Principals, even today, we do allow flexibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: We have about 800 students who were successfully transferred because they had made the wrong choice in the initial selection of schools and they now want to make a change.

sections.label: Students posted to choice schools
sections.summary: 95% of students are successfully posted to a school of their choice and 90% are in their top three choices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: For the Member's information, in our system today, 95% of our students are successfully posted to a school of their choice and 90% are actually in a school that is in their top three choices.

sections.label: Grassroots consultation and DSA system
sections.summary: Grassroots leaders will be consulted where applicable, and the Direct School Admission system recognises talents and achievements before PSLE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, perhaps the Acting Minister for Education can clarify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: We will consult grassroots leaders, where applicable, in policies where they have an impact on the locality and, in other circumstances, on a case-by-case basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: For the overall system, we do have the Direct School Admission (DSA) system that recognises talents and other achievements before PSLE.
